headline: Medium risk: Authelia can broker OAuth/ForwardAuth flows, but Awesome-prompts has no runtime surfaces, so pairwise harm is limited and mostly indirect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth, but awesome-prompts has no runtime I/O surfaces or execution path, so there is no documented channel for its content to inject instructions into Authelia by default. The pairwise pathway is therefore not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts is manually copied into a shared file or clipboard that Authelia parses as policy or config, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste prompt-library text into Authelia config files.
Review any copied text before using it in auth rules.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and can handle OAuth/ForwardAuth traffic, while awesome-prompts has no data classes touched and no runtime I/O. There is no shared workspace or sensitive-data path shown, so leakage is limited to unusual operator-mediated copying rather than a default pairwise flow.
conditions: IF the operator places secrets or user data into awesome-prompts content and then routes that content through Authelia-managed flows, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid storing secrets in prompt-library files.
Use separate repositories for auth config and prompt content.
Restrict Authelia logs to non-sensitive fields where possible.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound network calls and awesome-prompts is a static content repository with no write or network capability. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so direct capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because no locking or shared-write surface is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same filesystem path or git branch, conflict risk rises.
mitigations: Disable concurrent edits to shared config files.
Use a simple file lock if a shared path is unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can act as an identity gateway, but awesome-prompts is only a prompt list and does not produce authoritative operational facts or downstream actions. Without a documented pipeline from prompt content into Authelia decisions, cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than default automation.
conditions: IF prompt text from awesome-prompts is treated as policy input for Authelia without review, downstream mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Require human review before using prompt text in auth policy.
Keep prompt-library content out of production decision paths.
Document which inputs Authelia is allowed to trust.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, and the profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches. Because compliance risk would require a specific regulated data flow that is absent here, there is no plausible pairwise compliance violation to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later added to either agent's workflow, compliance review must be repeated.
mitigations: Record the data classes each agent may touch.
Add retention and residency notes before deployment.
Reassess if either agent begins handling regulated data.
